title: IPC: reject trailing bytes in CLI postcard frame decoder (P1 bug)

name: vb_cli
reason: Site of P1 bug and decode test scope; private decoder located here

summary: Change `if data.len() < payload_end` to `if data.len() != payload_end` and return Err(PostcardError::TrailingBytes). Adds the strict frame-length guarantee.
Add unit variant `TrailingBytes` to PostcardError and matching Display arm. Keeps parity with existing unit-shaped variants.
Re-export `PostcardError` (already done) covers the new variant by virtue of the enum shape; no re-export rename needed unless downstream wants `TrailingBytes` nameable from a public path.
`decode_postcard_json` calls `decode_postcard` via `?`; the new error propagates without any code change here. Verify Display for TrailingBytes is consistent with sibling arms.

Add `decode_rejects_trailing_bytes_after_valid_frame` (valid encode + 1 trailing byte -> Err(TrailingBytes)) and `decode_accepts_exact_length_frame` (no trailing bytes -> Ok). Use existing `encode_test_postcard` helper.

`OutputError::PostcardFrame(cli_postcard::PostcardError)` wraps the new variant; Display message consumes inner Display string. After adding the Display arm for TrailingBytes, `output_error_exit` will surface it through the existing path.
`assert_postcard_stdout` helper uses `cli_postcard::decode_postcard_json(&output.stdout)`; CLI encoded output never carries trailing bytes, so this test path stays green. Confirms not a regression.
`pub mod cli_postcard` already exposes module; no public-surface change required for the new enum variant.
No dependency change required; the bug fix is crate-local arithmetic plus one enum variant.

Add `prop_strict_length_no_trailing_bytes` property: for any trailing length n in `[1, 4096]`, valid_postcard ++ vec![0; n] -> Err(PostcardError::TrailingBytes). Strengthens roundtrip-style symmetry and guards against drift in future refactors.
